integrity: The proof uses the projective-line orthogonality involution, exact zero forcing polynomials of clique and balanced-biclique components, componentwise minimum rank, and a direct classification of equality cases as projective transversals.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to dimension two over finite fields.
The component decomposition is known from later finite-field dot-product work; the new strengthened content is the exact zero forcing polynomial, all minimum forcing sets, and real minimum rank.
The minimum-rank statement is over real symmetric matrices.
The q=2 case is a separate singleton-component boundary.
title: Zero forcing polynomial and minimum rank of two-dimensional finite-field total dot product graphs
